problem: pack masks stream lengths with & 0xFFFF instead of raising, so any input of 262144 bytes or more encodes to a block that silently decodes to different bytes of the same length.
unpack dropped the short-block and table-lengths-exceed-block checks, so truncated or malformed blocks decode silently to wrong output instead of raising ValueError.
pack no longer requires exactly 4 streams, so 5 streams silently merge the extra ones into stream 4 and fewer than 4 produce a block that unpacks to garbled streams.
split dropped the MIN_SPLIT_SIZE check, silently changing the public contract from raising ValueError on inputs under 4 bytes to accepting them.
The change removes four validation paths with no tests, and the repository has no test suite that would catch the 256 KiB truncation or the malformed-input regressions.
unpack hard-codes the table offset 6 instead of using TABLE_SIZE, so the format constant and the code can drift apart.
MAX_TABLE_LENGTH and MIN_SPLIT_SIZE are now unused while their values reappear as literals, implying limits the code no longer enforces.
